mn100:6.1: Ādibrahmacariya—the fundamentals, or principia, of the life divine.
mn100:42.2: The whole of this final passage is corrupt in the Text, the Commentary, and the Ṭīkā; the rendering here follows the sense given by the Commentary, taking aṭṭhitavataṁ/sappurisavataṁ as describing an endeavour that does not waver, of the sort found only in true men and Arahants.
mn100:42.4: The brahmin’s sudden change of subject is striking, as though the long story of the Bodhisatta’s striving and attainment of Buddhahood caused him to feel unsure of himself, and so he asked a question concerning his own tradition to gain reassurance.
